A: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is implicitly truthy whenever both `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set, with no explicit opt-in flag. An operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for any other webhook purpose silently activates the new public credential-injection endpoint and switches all OAuth token refreshes to the sync endpoint — a security-posture and behavior change triggered by environment presence rather than a deliberate feature flag that can be turned off without a code change.
B: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as `string | undefined` (the && of two env strings), not a boolean, so every `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)` and the webhook's `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` rely on implicit truthiness of a non-empty string. If either env var is set to a whitespace or placeholder value (e.g. copied from .env.example as `""` is left but a space is pasted in), the flag silently flips on and all token refreshes route to the (broken) sync path; a boolean coercion or explicit check would fail fast instead.
